newsitem.title: USA: Du Pont jury quizzed over tainting, seeks clarity.
newsitem.headline: Du Pont jury quizzed over tainting, seeks clarity.

text.p: The judge in the murder trial of millionaire chemicals heir John du Pont quizzed jurors on Thursday about possible tainting during the proceedings and once again explained fine points of Pennsylvania's murder law.

On their third day of deliberations, jurors were grappling with a complex array of choices among homicide charges against du Pont. They twice asked Court of Common Pleas Judge Patricia Jenkins to read to them definitions of the three degrees of homicide with which du Pont has been charged.
Jenkins reread the same definitions on Wednesday, the first full day of deliberations.
The six men and six women must reach a unanimous decision on one of eight possible verdicts, although du Pont's lawyers acknowledge he killed Olympic champion wrestler David Schultz on Jan. 26, 1996.
Du Pont's attorneys have sought a verdict of not guilty by reason of insanity.
The examination of possible tainting followed statements on Tuesday by an alternate juror that du Pont's unkempt appearance had been a topic of conversation while the trial was going on.
The alternate, Albert Allen, was excused with two other alternates before the start of deliberations on Tuesday.
Allen told reporters on Tuesday that jurors with whom he discussed the issue agreed that du Point's appearance was "a ploy."
But court spokesman John La Rosa said Jenkins was satisfied after polling the jurors that no conversations crossed into matters relating to the case, which could have led to a mistrial.
"They said they hadn't discussed the case ... prior to going into deliberations," La Rosa said.

On Tuesday, Allen told several reporters in a telephone conference call that he thought du Pont deserved a verdict of guilty of first degree murder but mentally ill, and that du Pont's dishevelled appearance was designed to bolster his insanity defence.
Throughout the 13 days of testimony, du Pont came to court with shaggy hair and an untrimmed beard and wearing sweat clothes with the logo of his Foxcatcher wrestling team.
"The jury was discussing this all along. We kept thinking that sooner or later he's going to come in clean-shaven. I think that was just a ploy, to tell you the truth," Allen said.
He said he had discussed it with some other jurors and there was general agreement that it was "a ploy."

The heir to the E.I. du Pont chemicals fortune is charged with first and third degree murder and voluntary manslaughter in the killing of Schultz at the wrestler's home on the du Pont estate. He also is charged with simple assault in allegedly pointing a gun at two eyewitnesses to the killing.
Aside from an insanity verdict, jurors could also find du Pont not guilty, guilty, or guilty but mentally ill on any of the homicide charges.
